title: Tobruk University Faculty of Nursing — curriculum and simulation map
scope: All eight instructor files. Source text preserved verbatim; added rationales and proposed adaptations explicitly separate.

maps.original: Stand in front of the sink; do not allow your uniform to touch the sink during the washing procedure.
maps.action: Approach sink without contacting basin with clothing.
maps.rationale: To prevent contamination of the uniform
maps.addedRationale: Use source rationale above; no new clinical claim.
maps.dependency: Before wetting; jewellery may be removed first.
maps.interaction: Move toward sink; collision boundary highlights uniform contact.
maps.feedback: Your uniform touched the sink. Step back to keep clothing away from contaminated surfaces.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Remove jewelry and watch. Allow plain wedding band to remain in place
maps.action: Remove watch and jewellery; confirm local ring policy.
maps.rationale:
Provides access to skin surfaces for cleaning.
Facilitates cleaning of fingers, hands, and
forearms.
maps.addedRationale: Use source rationale above; no new clinical claim.
maps.dependency: Before wetting; either order with stance.
maps.interaction: Drag watch/rings to clean storage tray.
maps.feedback: Jewellery obstructs cleaning. Remove it before wetting your hands.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Turn on water and adjust force. Regulate the temperature until water is warm.
maps.action: Turn on faucet; adjust comfortable water temperature and flow.
maps.rationale: Running water removes microorganisms. Warm water removes less of the natural skin oils.
maps.addedRationale: Proposed clarification: comfortable water, not a germ-killing temperature.
maps.dependency: Before wetting and soap.
maps.interaction: Operate tap handles and flow control.
maps.feedback: Reduce splashing and choose a comfortable temperature; hot water is unnecessary.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Wash hands and wrist area; keep hands lower than elbows.
maps.action: Wet hands/wrists; orient hands below elbows.
maps.rationale:
Water should flow from the least contaminated
to the most contaminated areas of the skin. Hands are considered more contaminated
than arms.
maps.addedRationale: Use source rationale above; no new clinical claim.
maps.dependency: After water; before soap.
maps.interaction: Visible forearms with wrist-height drag control.
maps.feedback: Keep hands below elbows and away from the basin.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Use about 1 teaspoon of liquid soap from dispenser or lather thoroughly with bar soap. Rinse bar soap before returning to the soap dish.
maps.action: Apply enough soap to cover hand surfaces; source also offers bar soap.
maps.rationale:
Lather facilitates removal of microorganisms.
Liquid soap harbors less bacteria than bar soap.
maps.addedRationale: Proposed alternative to fixed teaspoon: sufficient product per local instructions.
maps.dependency: After wetting; before rubbing.
maps.interaction: Depress dispenser; visible soap coverage.
maps.feedback: Too little soap leaves areas uncovered. Follow the approved product quantity.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: With firm rubbing and circular motion, wash hands, the palms and back of the hands, each finger, fingertips, knuckle wrist and forearms.
maps.action: Rub palms, backs, fingers, fingertips, knuckles, wrists and forearms as specified.
maps.rationale:
Friction mechanically removes microorganisms
from the skin surface. Friction loosens dirt
from soiled areas.
maps.addedRationale: Add explicit thumbs and interdigital coverage during faculty harmonisation.
maps.dependency: After soap; surface order flexible; all required areas before final rinse.
maps.interaction: Move visible hands through contact motions with coverage overlay.
maps.feedback: The backs of the fingers remain unwashed. Rotate the hands to cover that area.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Wash the forearms at least as high as contamination is likely to be present.
maps.action: Clean forearms to the likely level of contamination.
maps.addedRationale: Proposed rationale: remove contamination on exposed forearm without making full forearm scrubbing universal.
maps.dependency: During washing, before final rinse.
maps.safety: Scope of routine versus contaminated forearm cleaning
maps.interaction: Drag wash boundary on arm; contaminated areas remain visible.
maps.feedback: The marked contamination extends above the area you cleaned.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Continue this friction from 10-30 seconds
maps.action: Sustain rubbing; source specifies friction for 10–30 seconds.
maps.rationale: The longer you wash, the more germs are removed.
maps.addedRationale: Faculty must distinguish rubbing time from WHO total handwash duration of 40–60 seconds.
maps.dependency: During coverage; before final rinse.
maps.interaction: Coverage plus clock, not waiting alone.
maps.feedback: Time alone is insufficient; complete all hand surfaces before rinsing.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Use finger nails of the other hand or a clean wood stick
maps.action: Clean beneath fingernails; source suggests other fingernails or wood stick.
maps.rationale: To clean the area under fingernail.
maps.addedRationale: Proposed safe visual: fingertip rubbing; invasive scraping not implemented.
maps.dependency: During washing; before final rinse.
maps.interaction: Fingertip rotation on opposing palm; optional source method withheld.
maps.feedback: Avoid injuring the skin beneath nails. The instrument method requires faculty confirmation.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Rinse thoroughly.
maps.action: Rinse thoroughly without basin contact.
maps.rationale: To remove the soap from the skin.
maps.addedRationale: Use source rationale above; no new clinical claim.
maps.dependency: After adequate coverage and duration.
maps.interaction: Rotate hands under moving water; visible foam clears.
maps.feedback: Soap remains on your wrists. Rinse those areas without touching the basin.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Dry hands and wrist with paper towel/hand towel: turn off the faucet.
maps.action: Dry hands and wrists; shut off hand-operated faucet using a towel barrier.
maps.rationale:
Prevents contamination of clean hands by a
less clean faucet.
maps.addedRationale: Source rationale implies barrier; WHO explicitly specifies towel for faucet closure.
maps.dependency: Rinse then dry then protected faucet closure; foot-operated option differs.
maps.interaction: Dry each surface; carry towel to faucet; bin disposal.
maps.feedback: Your clean hand touched the faucet. Reclean the contaminated hands and use a towel barrier.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Wash your hands and dry.
maps.action: Clean and dry hands.
maps.rationale: To remove microorganisms from the hand, and to prevent the spread of infection.
maps.addedRationale: Use source rationale above; no new clinical claim.
maps.dependency: Before donning; prior completed appropriate hygiene accepted.
maps.interaction: Sink station or verified hygiene state.
maps.feedback: Gloves do not replace hand hygiene. Clean and dry your hands before donning.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Pull glove out of the box with one hand.
maps.action: Take first clean glove from box.
maps.addedRationale: Proposed rationale: limit unnecessary handling of clean supplies.
maps.dependency: After hand hygiene; before first donning.
maps.interaction: Pinch glove cuff at box.
maps.feedback: Handle the clean glove carefully and keep the box contents clean.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Slide glove onto other hand.
maps.action: Don first glove on opposite hand.
maps.addedRationale: Proposed rationale: fit enables coverage and dexterity.
maps.dependency: After taking first glove.
maps.interaction: Drag cuff over visible hand; align fingers.
maps.feedback: The cuff is not seated. Pull it over the wrist without tearing it.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Pull out another  with gloved hand
maps.action: Take second unused glove with newly gloved hand.
maps.addedRationale: Proposed rationale: distinguish a newly donned clean glove from a used glove.
maps.dependency: After first glove; before patient or dirty-surface contact.
maps.interaction: Touch box only while glove is still clean.
maps.feedback: This glove has touched a contaminated surface. Do not reach into the clean box with it.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Slide glove onto bare hand.
maps.action: Don second glove on remaining bare hand.
maps.addedRationale: Proposed rationale: complete coverage of both hands.
maps.dependency: After taking second glove.
maps.interaction: Drag cuff and guide fingers.
maps.feedback: The fingertips are not seated. Adjust the fit before patient care.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Interlace fingers
maps.action: Interlace fingers to adjust fit.
maps.rationale: To make gloves fit smoothly and comfortably
maps.addedRationale: Use source rationale above; no new clinical claim.
maps.dependency: After both gloves; before exposure.
maps.interaction: Visible finger interlacing; tear/fit inspection.
maps.feedback: Adjust the glove fingers; a torn glove must be replaced.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Removing of gloves
maps.action: Begin removal; keep bare skin away from outer contaminated surfaces.
maps.rationale: When removing gloves avoid touching the contaminated surfaces of the gloves with your bare hands.
maps.addedRationale: Use source rationale above; no new clinical claim.
maps.dependency: After simulated use; either hand can be removed first.
maps.interaction: Outer glove surface changes colour after simulated exposure.
maps.feedback: The coloured outer surface is contaminated. Keep it away from bare skin.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Grip glove at base of palm
maps.action: Grasp first glove outside near base of palm with other gloved hand.
maps.addedRationale: Use source rationale above; no new clinical claim.
maps.dependency: Before first peel.
maps.interaction: Select precise pinch point with visible gloves.
maps.feedback: Use the other gloved hand on the first glove outer surface.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Pull glove off inside out
maps.action: Peel first glove inside out and hold it in remaining glove.
maps.addedRationale: Holding first glove inside remaining gloved hand is an added explicit detail.
maps.dependency: After grasp; before bare fingers under second cuff.
maps.interaction: Continuous peel gesture changes glove inside/out orientation.
maps.feedback: Peel the glove inside out to contain the contaminated outer surface.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Slip bare fingers under wrist without touching the surface
maps.action: Slide bare fingers beneath second cuff, touching inner surface only.
maps.rationale: Avoid touching the contaminated surfaces of the gloves with your bare hands.
maps.addedRationale: Use source rationale above; no new clinical claim.
maps.dependency: After first glove off.
maps.interaction: Interior versus exterior cuff hit zones; contact location highlighted.
maps.feedback: Your bare fingers touched the outer cuff. This contaminated the skin at the highlighted point.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Push glove down and off
maps.action: Peel remaining glove off inside out around first glove.
maps.addedRationale: Proposed rationale: enclosing the first glove limits outer-surface contact.
maps.dependency: After bare fingers correctly placed.
maps.interaction: Pull cuff downward; nested glove bundle.
maps.feedback: Keep the contaminated glove surfaces enclosed while peeling.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Drop gloves in bag and seal tightly
maps.action: Dispose of glove bundle using approved waste route; source specifies sealed bag.
maps.addedRationale: Use source rationale above; no new clinical claim.
maps.dependency: After both removed; before final hygiene.
maps.interaction: Carry bundle to matching waste container.
maps.feedback: Do not put used gloves on clean equipment. Dispose of them in the designated waste container.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Drop the sealed bag into the trash
maps.action: Complete disposal; source says sealed bag into trash.
maps.addedRationale: Specific bag/seal/bin requirements depend on local waste policy.
maps.dependency: After containment; before final hygiene.
maps.interaction: Bin lid/pedal interaction.
maps.feedback: Complete disposal before cleaning your hands.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Carefully wash and dry hands
maps.action: Perform post-glove hand hygiene and dry as appropriate.
maps.rationale: To remove microorganisms from the hand
maps.addedRationale: Use source rationale above; no new clinical claim.
maps.dependency: After disposal; if contamination occurs earlier, interrupt and correct.
maps.interaction: Visible contamination clears only after effective hygiene.
maps.feedback: Gloves may leak or contaminate hands during removal. Clean your hands after disposal.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.feedback: That motion does not match Flexion. Compare the start and final positions; move within comfortable limits.

maps.original:
When you lift…
Position body close to object as possible
Straddle your legs, use leg power
maps.action: Move close, widen stance and lift a small object using legs.
maps.rationale: When you lift use the power of leg not your back to prevent strain at your back.
maps.addedRationale: Use source rationale above; no new clinical claim.
maps.dependency: Assess load/path before lift; foot placement order flexible.
maps.interaction: Visible nurse avatar; stance width, knee flexion and reach controls.
maps.feedback: The load is too far from your body. Move closer before lifting.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original:
When placing an object on a high shelf
Position yourself as close to the shelf as possible
maps.action: Approach shelf and place a light object without excessive reach.
maps.rationale: See you don’t have to reach to place the object to prevent strain on your muscle.
maps.addedRationale: Use source rationale above; no new clinical claim.
maps.dependency: Assess shelf height and clearance first.
maps.interaction: Drag feet closer; reach envelope.
maps.feedback: Your arm is overreaching. Reposition yourself or use an appropriate aid.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original:
For picking up objects off the floor use Golfer Tee Lift:
Hold on to something sturdy
Bend forward
Lift one leg for counter balance and relieves pressure from your lower back.
maps.action: Use supported golfer lift for a light floor item if balance allows.
maps.rationale: This will give counter balance and relieves the pressure on your lower back
maps.addedRationale: Use source rationale above; no new clinical claim.
maps.dependency: Stable support and light item first.
maps.interaction: One hand on stable support; opposite leg counterbalances.
maps.feedback: You have no stable support. Pause and choose a safe method for this item.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original:
Pivot, Don’t twist
Move your feet not your hips
maps.action: Pivot by moving feet while keeping trunk aligned.
maps.addedRationale: Use source rationale above; no new clinical claim.
maps.dependency: During direction change under load.
maps.interaction: Foot arrows and torso angle shown independently.
maps.feedback: Your hips stayed still while your trunk twisted. Move your feet to face the destination.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Push don’t pull.
maps.action: Push suitable wheeled load with clear path and appropriate force.
maps.rationale:
It’s easier to push than to pull
                 Pushing object whenever possible it is  
                 more control, and better body position, 
                 pushing means less injuries
maps.addedRationale: Use source rationale above; no new clinical claim.
maps.dependency: Assess equipment/load/route first.
maps.interaction: Trolley push/pull with visible posture.
maps.feedback: Check the route and load. Pushing is preferred here, but is not safe for every situation.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original:
When sitting at your desk:
Feet flat on the floor or foot rest
Elbows and knees at 90-100 degrees
Forearms and thighs parallel to the floor.
Lower back support
maps.action: Adjust chair, feet, lumbar support and forearms.
maps.rationale: To rest the leg and to make your body relax, and to prevent strain on your back
maps.addedRationale: Use source rationale above; no new clinical claim.
maps.dependency: Independent adjustments; evaluate combined final posture.
maps.interaction: Adjust seat/footrest and limb angles on seated avatar.
maps.feedback: Your feet are unsupported. Adjust seat height or add a footrest.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original:
Stretch periodically throughout the day:
Squeeze shoulder blades then relax.
Roll shoulders forward and backwards
When you stand stretch your back.
maps.action: Perform comfortable periodic shoulder and back movements.
maps.rationale: To promote relaxation of the muscle.
maps.addedRationale: Use source rationale above; no new clinical claim.
maps.dependency: During appropriate pause; stop if painful.
maps.interaction: Move shoulders/scapulae; gentle demonstration.
maps.feedback: Do not force a stretch into pain. Use comfortable movement.
maps.delivery: Design mapped; module not yet built

maps.original: Hand washing explain the procedure to the patient
maps.action: Clean hands and explain procedure; check understanding.
maps.addedRationale: Proposed educational rationale, absent from both source versions: Clean your hands before touching the patient. Explain the movement and obtain cooperation.
maps.dependency: Both before patient contact/movement. Explain and hygiene may swap.
maps.interaction: Sink/dispenser interaction plus patient conversation.
maps.feedback: Clean your hands before touching the patient. Explain the movement and obtain cooperation.
maps.delivery: Faculty-review manikin proof of concept

maps.original: Place the farther arm of the patient across his chest
maps.action: Prepare far arm across chest for side turn.
maps.addedRationale: Proposed educational rationale, absent from both source versions: Prepare and support the far arm before turning the trunk.
maps.dependency: After explanation/hygiene/assessment; limb preparation order flexible.
maps.interaction: Select far wrist; drag arm across chest.
maps.feedback: Prepare and support the far arm before turning the trunk.
maps.delivery: Faculty-review manikin proof of concept

maps.original: Place the near arm of the patient to his side
maps.action: Position near arm alongside body, clear of pressure.
maps.addedRationale: Proposed educational rationale, absent from both source versions: Keep the near arm clear of the body rather than trapped beneath it.
maps.dependency: Before turn; may occur before far arm.
maps.interaction: Select near wrist; slide to supported side position.
maps.feedback: Keep the near arm clear of the body rather than trapped beneath it.
maps.delivery: Faculty-review manikin proof of concept

maps.original: Farther leg across his near leg

maps.interaction: Select far knee; drag across with controlled arc.

maps.original: Place the hand of the nurse to the farther side of patients hips and shoulder

maps.dependency: After limb preparation, safe setup and assistance.
maps.interaction: Visible hands grasp drawsheet zones; direct shoulder traction blocked.
maps.feedback: Pulling on the shoulder can injure the patient. Use the agreed handling aid and assistance.
maps.delivery: Faculty-review manikin proof of concept

maps.original: Simultaneously turn the patient towards the nurse at the count of 3

maps.interaction: Count 1–2–3 then drag roll handle progressively to side.
maps.feedback: The body is not prepared. Secure the limbs and complete safety preparation before the count.
maps.delivery: Faculty-review manikin proof of concept

maps.original: Place a support pillow under patients arms and legs

maps.addedRationale: Proposed educational rationale, absent from both source versions: The upper leg is unsupported. Place support without losing alignment.
maps.dependency: After side turn; arm/leg pillow order flexible.
maps.interaction: Carry pillows to highlighted anatomical target zones.
maps.feedback: The upper leg is unsupported. Place support without losing alignment.
maps.delivery: Faculty-review manikin proof of concept

maps.original: Place the farther arm of the patient across his chest

maps.addedRationale: Proposed educational rationale, absent from both source versions: Prepare the far arm before rotating the trunk.
maps.dependency: Before first segment of prone roll; after assessment.

maps.feedback: Prepare the far arm before rotating the trunk.

maps.original: Place the near arm of the patient under his side

architecture: Scene and navigation
Shared room coordinates, articulated manikin and nurse, sink, bed, trolley, pillows, chair and equipment.
Free camera yaw/pitch plus walk controls and reachable object hit zones. Close-up technique camera remains available.
Current POC: movable 3D geometry with Canvas software renderer for devices without WebGL. Clinical realism comes from controllable anatomy and consequences.
Content contract
Module → scenarios → objects → actions → conditions → effects → source IDs → bilingual messages.
New modules reuse navigation, object interactions, feedback and debrief; only gestures/anatomy vary.
Original professor text and proposed additions remain separate. No runtime AI clinical advice.
Dependency graph
Hard prerequisites are risk-based; independent preparation actions commute.
Hygiene before contact, preparation before load, support after roll; limb and pillow order flexible.
No fixed global next-step index; predicate checks evaluate current world state.
Technique
Continuous gesture values and anatomical target zones.
Arm/leg/head angles, stance, bed height, sheet grip position and movement progress affect state.
Thresholds are interface tolerances, not clinical ROM prescriptions.
Reasoning coach
Seven explicit categories.
Correct; poor sequence; incomplete; technique error; safety-critical; unnecessary; acceptable alternative.
Guided shows rationale. Challenge logs details, but still halts unsafe simulated load.
Consequences
Errors change visible geometry or highlights.
Trapped arm red, twisted nurse lumbar highlight, missing pillow visible gap, edge zone red, contamination on hands.
Unsafe roll stops before load; learner may correct without restarting.
Assessment and debrief
Event log with time, action, category, rationale, source and assistance flag.
Compare final observable outcomes and log; omitted, sequence, technique and safety grouped separately.
No grade-led outcome. Demonstrated actions logged as assisted; fresh retry clears attempt only.
Languages
English and Arabic content keys; professional English terms retained.
Switch without losing camera, state or progress; RTL UI while spatial left/right remains consistent.
Faculty review Arabic clinical wording before student release.
Device and access
Responsive touch controls, keyboard equivalents and reduced-motion setting.
Large targets, tap/drag, keyboard/arrows, optional station navigation. No account or Moodle.
Canvas objects receive parallel accessible control labels; immersive 3D still benefits from sight.
Persistence and offline
Same-origin local assets plus PWA manifest and versioned service worker.
Cache only app assets; export debrief JSON on learner request; local attempt history optional.
First visit requires connection. No real patient data or student identifiers required.
M1 handwashing design
Source H01–H11; separate technique module.
Sink walk-up; visible hands; faucet/soap/rub coverage/rinse/dry/barrier states.
Timer plus surface coverage; contamination after clean faucet contact invalidates clean state.
M2 clean-gloving design
Source G01–G14; links to validated hygiene state.
Visible cuffs and inner/outer surfaces; continuous donning/peeling and disposal.
Bare-to-contaminated contact identifies exact finger/cuff event and requires hygiene.
M3 movement design
Source R01–R16; glossary corrections held for faculty.
Joint selection, constrained drag, start ghost, movement path and final pose.
Teach/assess direction as physical movement; no definition-only quiz.
M4 mechanics design
Source B01–B07.
Light-load lift, shelf reach, supported floor pick-up, pivot, trolley, chair, stretch.
Visible nurse joints and load distance; do not treat posture as substitute for patient-handling aids.
M5 turning implementation
Source T01–T17 plus explicit proposed safety additions.
Three independent manikin cases; individual limb preparation, sheet grip, count, progressive roll/slide and support.
Prone and manual-handling adaptations prominently pending faculty review.
M6 positioning design
Source P01–P13; shared bed/manikin rig.
Task prompt, bed pitch versus tilt, trunk orientation, joints and supports; final task rationale.
No automatic reward for a position name; evaluate assembled posture and support.
Faculty release process
Review register decisions, local aids/staffing, Arabic review, clinical demonstration and supervised learner pilot.
Record exact accepted changes by source ID; update content version and automated safety/dependency checks.
Current deliverable is a reviewable prototype, not a validated competency assessment.
